children: Amazon (AMZN) is adding a new manufacturing site in Greenwood, Indiana, with more than $100 million earmarked for the project as it expands domestic production of equipment used across its logistics and robotics operations.
AMZN shares were down 1% in morning trading Thursday.

The planned building will cover 585,000 square feet and is targeted to start operating by 2028. Amazon expects the project to create 300 skilled positions spanning manufacturing, engineering, quality control and program management.

The company said the site will produce equipment for its fulfillment and robotics network across North America. Average annual compensation for the new workforce is expected to approach $100,000, according to the release.

The investment adds to Amazon's manufacturing footprint in Indiana, where it said it has committed more than $40 billion since 2008 and supports over 27,000 direct jobs. The company also cited more than $230 billion invested in U.S. manufacturing since 2010.

Amazon is also expanding robotics production elsewhere in the country, including a Texas project unveiled in August, while operating two robotics manufacturing sites in Massachusetts. It will include robotic welding and automated assembly operations.

title: Amazon Stock Dips After $100 Million Indiana Manufacturing Push
